protocol.labels: issue_id is your own label. Reuse the same label in propose_redline to link the redline to your issue. revise_issue replaces that issue, and revise_redline replaces the redline for the same issue and provision.
protocol.escalation: Escalations are budgeted. Escalate departures from non-negotiable positions and requests beyond your authority. Both failing to escalate and over-escalating are scored.
protocol.negotiation: send_markup is answered deterministically by the counterparty: they accept, counter, or refuse. Accepting counterparty language you should not accept is scored. Closing every issue is not required — standing firm on a non-negotiable position and flagging it in your final summary is correct.

read_document.description: Read a document from the matter file, either in full or one numbered section.

section.description: Optional section number such as '4.2'. Omit for full text.

search_matter.description: Case-insensitive substring search across every document section.

query.description: Search phrase, three or more characters.

ask_client.description: Ask the client one natural-language factual question. Every question consumes budget, so ask only questions that could change the negotiating position.

escalate.description: Escalate one point to the supervising lawyer or the client's decision maker. Every escalation consumes budget, so escalate only departures from a non-negotiable position or requests that exceed your authority.

topic.description: Short label for the point escalated.

reason.description: Why this exceeds your authority or departs from the playbook.

submit_issue.description: Submit one material issue. Cite the single operative provision the issue targets as the FIRST citation, in the form '<document_id> §<section>'. Optional quotes must reproduce cited section text verbatim.

issue_id.description: Your own short label for this issue; reuse it in propose_redline.

citations.description: Provision citations such as 'msa §4.2'. Operative provision first.

quotes.description: Optional verbatim quotations supporting the issue. Text must appear verbatim in the cited section; paraphrase belongs in analysis.

revise_issue.description: Replace a previously submitted issue with a revised version. The issue_id must identify an existing issue. Only the latest version is used for scoring.

issue_id.description: Label of the issue to revise.

propose_redline.description: Propose replacement language for one section. Target the operative provision of the issue; link it to your submitted issue by reusing your issue_id label.

issue_id.description: Label of your submitted issue.

revise_redline.description: Replace the latest redline for an existing issue and provision. Only the latest version for that issue/document/section target is used for scoring.

send_markup.description: Send proposed language for one section to the counterparty and receive their response. The counterparty answers deterministically: they accept, counter with their own language, or refuse. Each markup consumes a negotiation round.

issue_id.description: Label of your submitted issue.

proposed_text.description: The language you are sending across the table.

accept_counterparty.description: Accept the counterparty's outstanding counter-proposal for one issue and close the point on their language. Accepting language you should not accept is scored.

issue_id.description: Your label for the issue whose counter you are accepting.

submit_final.description: Submit the final summary for the supervising lawyer and end the episode. Submit only after all issues and redlines are in.
